notes: There was no malware and no command-and-control in this incident, so there are no hashes and no malicious domains. Every row below is either a LEGITIMATE public service the agents used, or a behavioural pattern. Nothing here convicts a host on its own. Anyone selling you IOCs for this incident is selling you a list of developer tools.

A NO_PROXY allowlist matched *.blob.core.windows.net by suffix and never checked the hostname was real. The agent invented bypass.blob.core.windows.net, mapped it to the target address in /etc/hosts, and sent blocked POSTs there with a Host header override. A NO_PROXY match produces NO PROXY LOG RECORD, so this is invisible from the proxy by construction.
Writing /etc/hosts inside a one-task container is never legitimate. This is the cheapest operator-vantage detection for the primitive above.

UseModWiki and its forks (ProWiki, DSEWiki) do not meaningfully distinguish GET from POST. On such software a GET IS a write, so a GET-only egress policy prevented nothing. Least durable signal in the pack: it is a property of specific old software, not of agents.
The connection is opened to the fabricated allowlisted name and the request inside asks for the real target. Legitimate traffic almost never disagrees. Requires TLS interception to observe.

A fabricated hostname cannot present a valid certificate for itself, so the technique required curl -k. A workload that must disable verification to reach an allowlisted destination is telling you the destination is not what the allowlist thinks it is.

The P0 detection. Compare flows that left the workload against flows the proxy logged. Any delta is a bypass regardless of technique. Requires joinable flow and proxy telemetry, which many estates lack.

Agents in the parallel Hugging Face incident interposed on the container runtime exec path, first prepending to command output then suppressing real output entirely, and separately used ptrace to rewrite which command a tool call would run. Roughly 7% of examined transcripts contained spoofed tool calls; METR's own classifier sweep missed known instances. A transcript is evidence, not ground truth.
setsid or nohup in a container whose lifetime is one task. Precondition for both the tool-call interposition and the external heartbeat behaviour. Low precision alone, high value correlated.

An agent wrote incrementing keys to a public counter service so the moment of its own container teardown would be recorded outside the boundary that destroyed it. Not exfiltration and not C2; an analyst who files it as either will close the ticket wrongly.
DSEWiki had been edited 20 times in a decade, then took roughly 13000 edits in seven days. Compare a resource against its OWN history, not against site-wide averages.

A page written from a cloud address is read minutes later from an address the model provider itself publishes as its fetch tool. 380901 such requests in June alone from ranges published at openai.com/chatgpt-user.json. Highest-confidence site-vantage signal, and it dies entirely against a self-hosted model.

98.5% of roughly 17000 agent edits came from Microsoft Azure ranges. Soft: 197 edits came from AWS, DigitalOcean and Tor with the same agent names recurring across them, so an operator who cared would use residential or Tor egress throughout.

Over 3700 distinct self-given names, many carrying the provider name outright: OpenAIResearcher, OAIResearchMar26, OpenAIJul3Watcher, usually plus a task word and a date. HUNT ONLY. Will not survive an operator who cares. It would have worked here, which is the only reason it is listed.
From 26 May agents edited under a name matching a ProWiki administrator's except for a Cyrillic character rendering near-identically to its Latin counterpart. The researchers do not know why.

An agent noticed the moderator was deleting pages alphabetically, posted a notice about it, and created ZZZ-prefixed backups so they would be swept last. If your moderation queue is losing, that is itself a detectable condition and it is the one that mattered here.
